newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mobutu to shuffle government, supporter says.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu to shuffle government, supporter says.

text.p: President Mobutu Sese Seko told the country's leading politicians that Zaire -- with a chunk of its eastern territory in the hands of Rwandan-backed rebels -- needed to reshuffle the government, said a close supporter after talks with the ailing president on Thursday.

"The president was clear. A crisis government must be in place by midday Saturday, a government run by a credible man who has the support of the people," Bemba Saolona, a parliamentarian and a wealthy businessman, told Reuters.
There was no indication given who would lead the government.

Neither Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo, nor his rival for the job Etienne Tshisekedi of the radical opposition, attended the meeting in person although the prime minister was represented by the interior minister.

The talks followed Mobutu's return from four months in Europe where he had cancer surgery followed by rest. During his absence, Rwandan-backed Tutsi-led rebels seized a swathe of territory in the east.
Mobutu's first act after his return on Tuesday was to appoint a new army chief of staff -- General Mahele Bokoungo Lieko, a respected battlefield commander.
Kibassa Maliba, a member of the radical opposition, said talks would begin between opposition and Mobutu supporters on the new government. "We have 48 hours to agree on the names," he added.
Kitenge Jesus, a member of Mobutu's political family, said he expected no change at the head of the government. "You can't change the captain. Kengo wa Dondo is there, he will stay there," he said.
Mobutu, 66, has dominated national life in the sprawling and chaotic Central African nation since seizing power in 1965.

State television announced the appointment of General Mahele as chief of staff on Wednesday, saying the move was intended to help Zaire's demoralised army meet the challenge of the Tutsi-led revolt in the east.

Mahele, sacked as army chief of staff by Mobutu in 1993, snuffed out a revolt by rebel leader Laurent Kabila in 1984 and helped fight Tutsi rebels who challenged Rwanda's late Hutu president Juvenal Habyarimana in 1990.
His nomination was "part of a restructuring of the Armed Forces of Zaire with the view to putting them on a war footing and improving their efficiency", the television said.
Mobutu, who had surgery for prostate cancer in Switzerland in August, returned to a rapturous welcome on Tuesday and pledged to "restore Zaire's tarnished image".
